_comment: The report's cumulative section, one entry per aggregate. Each entry names the tree it describes, so a figure that has fallen behind the branch says so in the rendered table instead of relying on someone remembering. `file` is a perf/scripts/compare_screen.py output under perf/baselines/; `figures` is for an aggregate that is not screen output.

aggregates.label: Read loop, 57 scenarios
aggregates.note: on one host with the arms alternated and both trees proved different by content hash. The scenario set includes the 18 row-rendering requests that finding 44 showed were never measured, and **the branch changes not one query on any of them** -- yet their wall clock falls a median 18.6%, because the work removed is Python rather than SQL. The document half of a list view is unchanged at a median -1.3%

aggregates.label: Whole-workflow apply, 11,572 objects
aggregates.coverage: 11,572 objects across 68 models, row counts identical on both arms
aggregates.note: both arms from a database reset to the same empty template, trees proved different by content hash, the client driven from a second host so it cannot compete with the stack it is measuring, and every run created exactly 11,572 objects and ended with identical row counts -- 536 devices, 1,616 interfaces, 1,648 cables -- with zero client failures, so the arms provably did the same work. **Of the 720 seconds saved, 4.1 are database execution**. Queries and database time are the median of two branch arms against one stock arm, which settles them: the two branch arms agreed to 0.07% on queries, and `apply_arm.sh` records that one run per arm settles the deterministic half. **The wall-clock figure is provisional.** It rests on one stock arm, run in the order branch, branch, stock rather than three alternating rounds, and this branch's own record is why that matters -- a 2ms and an 11% regression both dissolved on a third round. Two more stock arms with the ordering reversed are needed before it is quotable. The stock arm hashed `0e1d03a4e` rather than next's own `e308df687`, because a path-scoped checkout cannot delete finding 22's migration; it is inert during an apply, and `arm_control.sh` now removes such files

_stock_comment: The commit the stock arm of every aggregate here was measured against. verify_report.py asserts the ref still resolves to it: if next moves, the figures describe a tree that no longer exists and want re-measuring, which should fail a check rather than be noticed by someone eventually.
